title: Police tighten curbs outside Abhishek Banerjee's home as state challenges his court protection
dek: After an overnight clash outside the Trinamool leader's Kalighat home, Kolkata Police are enforcing a prohibitory order there. The state government has asked the Supreme Court to set aside the High Court protection he holds in three cases.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Kolkata Police are strictly enforcing a prohibitory order outside Trinamool Congress general secretary Abhishek Banerjee's home in Kalighat after an overnight clash between Trinamool and BJP supporters there, and the West Bengal government has asked the Supreme Court to set aside the protection from police action that the Calcutta High Court gave him in August.

Mr Banerjee has accused BJP supporters of attacking his home at about 2 am on Saturday, alleging stone-pelting and firing "right under the watch of the Kolkata police". A BJP minister dismissed his account. Police have not confirmed that stones were thrown or shots fired, and no arrests had been reported by Saturday afternoon.

## The prohibitory order

An order under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), which allows police to bar gatherings, has been in force in the area since 16 October for two months, according to reports. After the overnight clash, police decided to enforce it strictly. Reports said it covers the stretch from Kalighat Bridge along the Ganga ghats via Balaram Bose Ghat, School Row, Harish Mukherjee Road and Hazra Road to the area in front of Mr Banerjee's house, and is meant to stop crowds gathering outside it. Kolkata Police had not issued a public statement on the clash by Saturday afternoon.

## The Supreme Court petition

The state government filed its appeal in the Supreme Court on Friday, according to reports. It challenges an order of 25 August in which Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya of the Calcutta High Court protected Mr Banerjee from coercive action until 30 November in cases registered at the Bhowanipore, Kalitala and Bishnupur police stations, after rejecting the state's request for a stay. Mr Banerjee had told the High Court that 16 FIRs had been filed against him since the change of government and that they were politically motivated. The judge observed that his direct link to the Kalitala and Bishnupur incidents, which date to 2017 and 2020 and were not reported to police at the time, was not clear, reports said.

The state argues, according to reports, that the allegations are serious, that Mr Banerjee could have sought anticipatory bail in each case, that several FIRs cannot be challenged together in a single petition, and that no accused should get "blanket protection". The Supreme Court is expected to hear the appeal after its Diwali break; no date has been listed. Mr Banerjee has not responded publicly to the petition, though in his overnight posts he thanked the High Court and the Supreme Court, sarcastically, for "remaining mute spectators".

## What each side says

According to Mr Banerjee's posts and reports from the scene, a crowd gathered outside his residence in Kalighat, south Kolkata, after midnight. Trinamool workers alleged that BJP supporters shouted "chor, chor" (thief, thief) at about 2.30 am, that a clash followed, that cutouts and banners of Mr Banerjee were damaged and that several Trinamool supporters were hurt, according to one report. None of the injuries has been confirmed by police or hospitals. Reports said there was a confrontation between supporters of the two parties before police intervened to separate them.

Mr Banerjee came down from the house and sat outside in protest from about 2.45 am to 6 am, one report said, and had a heated exchange with police officers. He went back inside after police asked him to and a Trinamool worker who had been detained was released, according to the same report. He said police and the administration had failed to act. On Saturday morning he posted two videos: one shows a man hitting a gate with a bamboo stick, the other a crowd throwing objects at the building while a few police officers push people back. He said the attack came after "two days of continuous recce". He described it as "the seventh attempt on my life in the last six months".

Saturday is Mr Banerjee's birthday, and supporters had gathered outside his home. Panchayat Minister Dilip Ghosh of the BJP, speaking to reporters in New Town, mocked what he called a politician's birthday "being celebrated on the footpath" and said: "If someone creates a disturbance, there is bound to be a backlash." He asked who had "the time to kill Abhishek Banerjee" and accused Trinamool of misleading people. Neither the BJP's state unit nor Kolkata Police had issued a formal statement on the incident by Saturday morning.

Trinamool chairperson and former chief minister Mamata Banerjee, Mr Banerjee's aunt, accused the BJP on Saturday afternoon of sending "a gang of thugs" to his home between 2 am and 3 am. "There is complete hooliganism going on," she said, according to reports. She said permission for traditional local Kali Pujas had been withdrawn while a new puja was allowed on the main road, and that local clubs had been stopped from functioning overnight. "Go ahead - run your bulldozers over us," she said. Trinamool MP Kirti Azad said the party had written to the Lok Sabha Speaker, that CCTV footage showed people armed with stones and sticks attacking for 30 to 45 minutes, and that police had made no arrests. The footage he described has not been released in full, and police had not responded to the claims by Saturday afternoon.

## The 'surveillance' complaint

The incident came hours after Mr Banerjee alleged on Friday that "a few unidentified individuals" had been watching his office and residence for two days, and that when confronted they had claimed to be police officers. He posted the registration number of a motorcycle he said they used, asked "who authorised this surveillance and for what purpose", and sought an inquiry from Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, the Union Home Ministry, Kolkata Police and West Bengal Police. There has been no public response to that request.

## Background

Relations between the two parties have grown more bitter since the BJP won the Assembly election in May, ending 15 years of Trinamool rule, with Suvendu Adhikari as chief minister. On 29 October Mr Banerjee warned police officers that they would face action once his party returned to power, saying they were framing Trinamool workers in false cases; Mr Adhikari responded by challenging him to contest the 2029 Lok Sabha election from Diamond Harbour. Trinamool has accused the state government of targeting its leaders and offices, and the BJP has accused Trinamool of stoking unrest. The accounts of Saturday's incident could not be independently verified.

## What happens next

Mr Banerjee has asked for an inquiry. The High Court's protection runs until 30 November unless the Supreme Court intervenes earlier. Any statement from Kolkata Police on what happened outside the house, and on Mr Banerjee's surveillance complaint, would be the first official account of the night.
